entries.name: diagnose-windows-sandbox-acl
entries.description: Use on Windows for unexpected DSH sandbox access denials: workspace writes or listing fail, or an ordinarily readable path cannot be read. tools.name: asset_create
tools.description: Create a draft asset and validate it physically (compiles, has mass, rests without tipping or sinking when dropped). Give either a generator with params (generators: building {width, depth, height}, counter {width, depth, height}, dining_table {width, depth, height, mass}, cabinet_with_drawer {width, depth, height, drawer_height}, cup {radius, height, mass, fragile}, plate, bowl, steward_bot) or an authored template. An entity template is a World State Entity with id "w:template" and an identity pose: {id, role: environment|object|robot|actor, category: {value}, pose: {value: {p: [0,0,0], q: [1,0,0,0]}}, body: {kind: "rigid", root: {value: fixed|planar|free}, links: [{id, name, geometry: {collision: [{kind: "primitive", shape: box|sphere|cylinder|capsule, size: full extents in metres (box [x,y,z], cylinder [r, length]), pose: {p, q}, rgba}], visual: [...]}, inertial: {value: {mass}}, material: {value: {friction, fragility}}, affordances: [{value: "graspable"}]}], joints: [{id, parent, child, type: {value: fixed|revolute|prismatic}, origin: {value: {p, q}}, axis: {value}, limits: {value: {lo, hi}}, q: {value: [0]}, qd: {value: [0]}}]}}. The origin sits on the floor at the footprint centre. Read an existing asset with asset_get for a full example. Nothing is published until asset_publish.

params.description: Generator parameters as a JSON object.

template.description: Authored entity template as a JSON object.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a local direct child's conversation later with send_message. External executions stop permanently and cannot receive follow-ups. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: observer_report
tools.description: Read how accurate each robot's own world model is compared with the true World State: object recall, false detections, position error, uncertainty calibration (NEES) and self-localisation error.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:/...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Provide `description` before `command` in the arguments. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. Do not assign to automatic variables such as `$HOME`; variable names are case-insensitive, so `$home` is the same read-only variable. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

Spec: {name, entities: [{id: "w:<unique>", asset, at: {x, y, yaw}} or {id, asset, on: "w:<support id placed earlier>", offset: [dx, dy], yaw}], regions: [{id, label, polygon: [[x, y], ...]}]}. Place robots with at; place objects on furniture with on.

tools.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

tools.name: slarm_cancel
tools.description: Explicitly cancel a reconstruction submitted by this local SLARM store. Closing a browser or aborting polling does NOT cancel it. cancelling means cleanup is ongoing; only cancelled=true confirms cancellation. Continue slarm_status if necessary.

reconstruction_id.description: Actual rec_ id returned by slarm_reconstruct. Never invent ids.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for a terminal state (0-20 by default); omitted means one immediate query. Does not cancel remote work.

tools.description: Read current SLARM readiness, API version, output choices and limits before uploading. This does not run reconstruction.

tools.description: Read SLARM dataset validation. validating means wait; ready allows reconstruction; invalid means stop and report issues. No work is submitted.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for a terminal state (0-20 by default); omitted means one immediate query. Does not cancel remote work.

tools.name: slarm_download
tools.description: Download selected artifact ids from a successful result. Select ALL pointcloud artifacts for all windows plus desired videos. Saves beneath the configured stateDir, verifies bytes and SHA256, reuses verified files and returns absolute paths. There is no all-results ZIP. Download failures do not invalidate completed reconstruction; retry this operation.

reconstruction_id.description: Actual rec_ id returned by slarm_reconstruct. Never invent ids.

artifact_ids.description: Nonempty unique artifact ids returned by slarm_result; never filenames or arbitrary URLs.

tools.name: slarm_reconstruct
tools.description: Submit a READY SLARM dataset. Range [start,end) must contain 16-256 time frames, within the dataset. Exactly 16 frames gives one model window; each uses offsets 0,5,10,15 across three cameras. Returns reconstruction_id and status, NOT completion. Use slarm_status then slarm_result. For point clouds and previews request pointcloud, rgb_video and diagnostic_video. No local SLARM/NPU environment is needed.

request_key.description: Stable operation key, 8-128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse EXACTLY for retries, including after disconnects. Use a new key only for intentional new work.

outputs.description: Nonempty unique export choices. Depth/semantic/scene_flow share render_arrays artifacts.

evaluate.description: Request metrics against available reference data; omitted is false. Missing GT metrics remain null.

gaussian_stride.description: Only with gaussians: integer 1-256; omitted follows server default 16. Controls exported snapshots, not model input sampling.

tools.name: slarm_result
tools.description: Read and save a successful reconstruction manifest. Returns predictions, coordinates, actual input/output counts, warnings and ALL artifact ids. Only completed=true permits reporting reconstruction complete. Point counts are not object counts; quality_status=ok is not accuracy validation. No instance tracks or fused MuJoCo scene are provided. Large arrays stay in files; use slarm_download selectively.

reconstruction_id.description: Actual rec_ id returned by slarm_reconstruct. Never invent ids.

tools.name: slarm_status
tools.description: Query reconstruction progress, optionally waiting. queued/starting/running/finalizing/cancelling/recovering are not completed. On succeeded fetch slarm_result; on failed/cancelled/expired stop. Progress at 100% alone is not success.

reconstruction_id.description: Actual rec_ id returned by slarm_reconstruct. Never invent ids.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for a terminal state (0-20 by default); omitted means one immediate query. Does not cancel remote work.

tools.name: slarm_upload
tools.description: Upload a local Waymo or slarm_scene_v1 ZIP to SLARM. Requires three synchronized RGB cameras, calibration and known poses. The path is on this DSH host beneath inputRoot, not the remote server. Returns dataset_id; query validation before reconstruction. This uploads file contents to the configured server. Aborting the HTTP call does not delete accepted data.

archive_path.description: ZIP path relative to inputRoot, or an absolute path within it.

request_key.description: Stable operation key, 8-128 letters/digits or ._:-. Reuse EXACTLY for retries, including after disconnects. Use a new key only for intentional new work.

format.description: Use slarm_scene_v1 for world_capture exports. Omitted means legacy waymo_slarm_v1.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool starts an independently managed subagent and immediately returns its id. The runtime notifies you when it finishes. The child reports results with `send_message`; use `send_message` to steer it while running or continue its conversation after it finishes.

cwd.description: Initial child working directory. Relative paths use your current directory; omitted inherits it. Later directory changes in either agent are independent.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. While work remains, keep the todos being worked on `in_progress`, several only when work runs in parallel. Mark each todo `completed` as soon as it is done.

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the current goal.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

action.description: edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. complete and blocked are also allowed during an automatic continuation of this goal; blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Required only with action blocked: the concrete condition that persisted across rounds and blocks progress.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch the content of a specific HTTP(S) URL and return it decoded to text.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: 1–4 search queries; their results are merged.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

tools.name: working_directory
tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths use the current directory. Existing shells and running processes keep their own directories.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.name: world_cameras
tools.description: Read or switch single/triple cameras for a world robot. Triple mode adds left/right views with the original calibration. During recording mode changes are rejected. Status includes the latest capture; inspect it after a lost start response before retrying.

mode.description: Omit to read current mode and latest capture.

tools.name: world_capture
tools.description: Record a synchronized three-camera sequence in simulation time. Requires triple mode and a running clock. Does not move the robot. Poses are simulation ground truth, not SLAM estimates. Returns capture_id, not a finished ZIP. Poll world_capture_status; upload only a succeeded archive_path using slarm_upload format=slarm_scene_v1. HTTP abort does not cancel recording; use world_capture_cancel. After a lost response query world_cameras before retrying.

frames.description: Integer 16-256 time frames; default 16, yielding 48 images.

fps.description: Simulation-time rate, 1-30; period must align with physics steps. Default 10.

tools.name: world_capture_cancel
tools.description: Request cancellation of one local capture. Poll world_capture_status until cancelled; cancelling alone is not confirmation. This does not cancel a separately submitted SLARM reconstruction.

tools.name: world_capture_status
tools.description: Read capture progress; wait_seconds may wait 0-20 seconds. Failed/cancelled recordings have no usable ZIP. Capture handles expire on host restart; completed ZIP files persist. Report errors, never substitute duplicated frames.

tools.name: world_catalog
tools.description: List saved scenes and scenarios.

tools.name: world_clock
tools.description: Pause or resume the simulation, or set its speed factor.

value.description: Speed factor for speed, for example 2.

tools.name: world_edit
tools.description: Change the running World State without stopping the episode (robots keep working and must notice the change themselves). move: relocate an object or piece of furniture; objects resting on moved furniture move with it. spawn: add a new entity from a published asset (see asset_search). remove: delete an entity; objects resting on it fall. Place with x/y (floor position in metres, world frame) or with on (support entity id, e.g. "w:table") plus offset_x/offset_y in the support frame. yaw in radians; move keeps the current yaw when omitted. Robots, the building and objects a robot is holding cannot be edited; an edit that would interpenetrate another entity is rejected and leaves the world unchanged. Read world_scene first for ids and positions.

entity.description: Entity id, e.g. "w:cup-1"; for spawn a new unique id.

asset.description: Published asset name for spawn, e.g. "cup".

on.description: Support entity id to place on, e.g. "w:sideboard".

offset_x.description: x offset on the support, in the support frame (default 0).

offset_y.description: y offset on the support, in the support frame (default 0).

tools.name: world_scene
tools.description: Read the true current World State: every entity with its exact pose and the relations between entities (what rests on what, what is held). This is ground truth that robots cannot see.

detail.description: Return the full SceneState instead of a compact listing (default false).

tools.name: world_status
tools.description: Read the loaded scenario, simulation time and speed, entities, robots (what they hold) and recent world events such as grasps.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.
